definitions.explanation: The organized, interrelated whole formed by a country's laws — the way its statutes, codes, and regulations fit together as a structured system.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{法体系|ほうたいけい}を{学|まな}ぶ。
{国|くに}によって{法体系|ほうたいけい}は{大|おお}きく{異|こと}なる。
examples.english: Legal systems differ greatly from country to country.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{技術|ぎじゅつ}の{登場|とうじょう}で、{既存|きそん}の{法体系|ほうたいけい}では{対応|たいおう}しきれない{問題|もんだい}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: With the emergence of new technologies, problems that the existing legal system cannot fully handle are increasing.

notes:
Composed of {法|ほう} (law) + {体系|たいけい} (system, organized structure). Refers to a body of law viewed as a coherent, interconnected whole rather than as individual statutes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {法体系|ほうたいけい}を{整|ととの}える: to put a legal system in order
- {既存|きそん}の{法体系|ほうたいけい}: the existing legal system
- {大陸法|たいりくほう}{系|けい}の{法体系|ほうたいけい}: a civil-law-based legal system

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {法制度|ほうせいど}: legal system (as institutions and their workings) — overlaps closely, but emphasizes the institutional side
- {六法|ろっぽう}: the Six Codes — the core statutes at the center of Japan's legal system
